tldr: CodeTree is an agent-guided tree search framework that uses a heterogeneous tree structure with specialized LLM agents to explore diverse coding strategies and iteratively refine solutions, achieving top results on multiple code generation benchmarks.
contributions: A unified tree-based search framework (CodeTree) for efficient exploration of code generation search spaces across different stages
Four specialized agents (Thinker, Solver, Debugger, and Critic) that collaborate through tree expansion guided by both execution-based and AI feedback
Demonstration of significant performance gains across 7 benchmarks, achieving top results on HumanEval, MBPP, and CodeContests
methods: CodeTree builds a heterogeneous tree for each coding problem, where the root is the problem specification and subsequent nodes are generated code solutions. A Thinker Agent generates diverse high-level coding strategies, a Solver Agent implements strategy-specific code candidates, and a Debugger Agent refines solutions using execution feedback and reflections from the Thinker. A Critic Agent dynamically guides tree expansion by scoring nodes based on test case execution and strategy adherence, then deciding to Refine (continue exploring), Abort (prune), or Accept (terminate) each node.
results: Using GPT-4o as the base model, CodeTree achieved pass@1 scores of 95.1% on HumanEval, 98.7% on MBPP, and 43.0% on CodeContests. On CodeContests, this represents a 22.4% performance gain over the Resampling baseline. CodeTree outperformed all baselines in 4 out of 5 benchmarks for both GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4o. CodeTree-BFS consistently outperformed CodeTree-DFS. For larger width (w=5) and smaller depth (d=2), performance improved on harder problems like CodeContests. However, on Llama-3.1-8B, Resampling achieved the best results on 4 benchmarks, indicating small models may not suit multi-agent frameworks.
limitations: Small language models (e.g., Llama-3.1-8B) may not be suitable for multi-agent frameworks like CodeTree, as they struggle to follow task-specific roles and instructions with sufficient accuracy
The method struggles with very difficult/competition-level problems
Inference time requires limiting the number of exploration steps to avoid large computation overhead
DFS search depth beyond d=3 did not significantly boost performance
